subject.title: [AI] fix(memory): backfill provider.model with resolved model name in…

question: Should OpenClaw accept this source-layer normalization of empty memory `provider.model` values before the broader memory provider auto-detection work lands?
rationale: The patch is narrow and appears correct, but it changes the model identity used by persisted memory metadata and vector lookup when adapters return an empty model, which repository policy treats as compatibility-sensitive.

options.title: Land the backfill now
options.body: Accept the narrow normalization because it fixes the broken empty-model state at the provider creation boundary without adding new config or downstream fallbacks.

options.title: Require full persisted-index proof
options.body: Ask for a live upgraded-index reindex plus `memory_search` transcript before merge if maintainers want stronger end-to-end storage proof.

options.title: Bundle with provider policy
options.body: Pause this PR if maintainers want the source backfill to land only with the broader auto-provider migration decision.

recommendation.title: Land the backfill now
recommendation.body: Accept the narrow normalization because it fixes the broken empty-model state at the provider creation boundary without adding new config or downstream fallbacks.

likelyOwner.reason: The decision sits at the provider adapter boundary and persisted memory identity behavior, both areas tied to steipete's feature history.
